sources.title: Telehouse: Telehouse inaugure un nouveau datacenter sur son campus de Francfort et poursuit son développement en Europe (communiqué de presse, 1 September 2026)
sources.summary: Telehouse's press release (Paris, September 2026; page dated 1/09/2026) announces the official opening of its new data centre, Building N (le bâtiment N), on its Frankfurt campus. It says the building was put into service this summer, is the seventh data centre built on the site, and was fully let before it opened. Building N has 2,200 m2 of colocation space on three levels, 3.6 MW of IT capacity on a 4.5 MW electrical infrastructure, a PUE of 1.25, renewable electricity only, N+1 power and N+2 cooling redundancy, DRUPS and up to 48 hours of generator autonomy, with access to more than 400 carriers and cloud providers and a direct DE-CIX connection. Design began in 2022, construction finished in 2025 and the building was commissioned progressively during the first half of 2026. The release quotes the managing director of KDDI Europe.
sources.date_semantics: The page shows 1/09/2026 and its JSON-LD gives datePublished 2026-09-01T13:01:27Z and dateModified 2026-09-01T13:25:13Z; the post sitemap lastmod is the same. 1 September 2026 is used as the publication date and as the observation date of the operating statement. It is not the commissioning day, which the release gives only as summer 2026 (progressive commissioning in the first half of 2026). The executive quoted is identified here by role only.

Unit 1 is a 4,288 sq m GIA, 15 MW building; Units 2-8 are 13,961 sq m GIA, 60 MW buildings, each with a data hall 96 m wide and 64.5 m long, offices and diesel standby generator enclosures. The site is 32.3 ha of former MOD land south of Graven Hill and St David's Barracks; existing buildings have been demolished and the Employment Access Road to Pioneer Road and the A41 is built. It records outline permission 22/01829/OUT (B8 up to 104,008 sq m GIA) approved 10 October 2023, two pre-application discussions for an eight-data-centre scheme, and addresses third-party arguments that data centres are sui generis rather than B8, concluding that the scheme falls within the outline permission.
